_why: Per-package floors, not a total. Measured on main d2928b2 the total sat at 50.3% while
internal/content had fallen from 43.9% to 34.7% — nine points of regression that a
total-only gate reports as no change, because other packages grew at the same time.
An average is the wrong instrument for 'did anything get worse'.
Each floor is the measured value rounded DOWN to a whole percent, so a refactor that
shifts one statement does not fail the build. The cost, stated rather than hidden: a
real regression smaller than the distance to the next whole percent passes. Raise a
floor when coverage improves; the ratchet only tightens if someone tightens it.
Regenerate the numbers with: python3 scripts/coverage_gate.py --print-floors
Check the tree with:         python3 scripts/coverage_gate.py

github.com/KlangHaus/resonans/internal/p: 0% here is misleading on purpose and must not be 'fixed' by deleting a build tag.
This package IS covered — by the integration cells in rls_integration_test.go, which
carry //go:build integration and need a real postgres. The `Tenant isolation` check runs
them; `Lint + Test`, which this gate reads, does not. So the floor is 0 and the real
guard is elsewhere. Anyone raising this number by moving those tests out from behind
the tag would make `go test ./...` require a database.
github.com/KlangHaus/resonans/cmd/resona: Argument parsing and process exit. Reachable only by running the binary, which the
container HEALTHCHECK and the deploy do. UNMEASURED rather than covered: nothing here
github.com/KlangHaus/resonans/internal/o: OTel wiring. Exercised in every test that boots the app, but it reports 0% because
the assertions are about the app, not about the exporters. UNMEASURED.

gate was blind to until this package existed. A floor of 0 is correct here and means

postgres in the `Tenant isolation` check, which is the only measurement that means
github.com/KlangHaus/resonans/internal/d: Holds one file: the guard that keeps the shipped deploy SQL from echoing secrets.
It has tests and NO statements of its own — the same third output shape internal/apidocs
has, which this gate prints as `coverage: [no statements]`. A floor of 0 is correct and
means 'nothing to cover', not 'untested': the guard IS the test. What is genuinely
unmeasured here is the end-to-end canary against a real postgres, which is by hand until
CI has a database (KH-1220) — this package only reads the files.
github.com/KlangHaus/resonans/docs/api: Holds one file: an embed directive and a var, and ZERO functions — so this is a
fourth output shape again, `[no test files]`, and there is nothing a test could
call. A floor of 0 means 'nothing to cover', not 'untested'.
The DOCUMENT it embeds is measured, in two places: the drift cell in
internal/apidocs compares it to the registered routes, and a cell in
internal/apiref asserts the bytes served over /docs/v1/openapi.yaml are the same
bytes as the file on disk — so an embed replaced by a stale copy fails there.
